analysis.title: Alphabet's full stack strategy: hard to copy, harder to pay for
key_insights: Alphabet owns all four layers needed to deliver AI (chips, cloud, models, distribution), while most rivals own two or three and rent the rest. Each layer feeds the next: TPUs lower Cloud compute cost, Cloud trains and serves Gemini, Gemini reaches users through Search, Android and Chrome, and scale lowers TPU cost.
Google Cloud revenue doubled to USD 30.7bn in Q3 2026 at a 36.2% operating margin, with a USD 561bn backlog. Cloud is now above USD 120bn annualised revenue with USD 11.1bn of Q3 operating profit.

TPU systems now have more than 100 significant external customers, including Anthropic, Apple, Meta, Citadel Securities and Jump Trading. They are served in Google Cloud, in customers' own data centres, at Oracle and through Crux AI, a joint venture with Blackstone.

Alphabet sells complete TPU systems with networking, storage and software, not only cloud access. TPU system sales were a 'meaningful contributor' to Q3 Cloud revenue, but Google Cloud Platform services made up the vast majority.

The 8th generation TPU launched this year offers up to 2.7x better training performance and 80% better inference price-performance than the previous generation (company-reported). Cost advantage matters most for Search, where an AI answer earns less than a page of links.

Q3 2026 free cash flow was minus USD 9.1bn (operating cash flow USD 42.3bn less capex USD 51.4bn), or about minus USD 3.9bn excluding the USD 5.2bn EU fine. Trailing twelve-month free cash flow fell to USD 19.7bn.
Capex was 40% of revenue in Q3 2026, up from 23% a year earlier. Revenue grew 25% while capex grew 114%. Guidance for 2026 capex is USD 195-205bn, with a significant increase expected in 2027.

About 65% of capex goes to servers and networking with six-year lives, so depreciation (up 49% in Q3) will keep rising. Purchase commitments are USD 924bn and leases not yet started are USD 152bn, though some contracts allow lower volumes.
TPU inventory rose from USD 2.4bn at end 2025 to USD 13.3bn. Cash returns only on delivery and billing, mostly in 2027, so each new contract consumes cash before it returns any.
Alphabet repurchased no shares in the first nine months of 2026 versus USD 39.8bn a year earlier. Dividends are the only remaining direct shareholder return.

Cloud margin of 36.2% compares with 40.7% for Google Services, but Cloud excludes USD 7.7bn of shared AI costs, faces AWS and Azure, sells to a few large clients who can negotiate or build their own chips, and needs heavy capital per dollar of profit. Syz argues the market will not pay the same multiple for Cloud profit as for Search profit.
Just over 55% of the USD 561bn Cloud backlog should convert to revenue within 24 months. Cloud margin faces headwinds in Q4 as rented capacity ramps up.
Syz conclusion: the full stack protects Alphabet's strategic position more than it answers the market's demand for cash. Whether it can deliver returns comparable to Search is unproven.

market_movers.rationale: The full stack is a hard-to-copy response to the AI threat on Search and the backlog suggests customers are buying in. Returns, cash flow and buybacks remain unproven, so the note gives no rating or target.

earnings_insights: Alphabet Q3 2026 (reported): Google Cloud revenue USD 30.7bn, roughly double the prior year, operating margin 36.2%, operating profit USD 11.1bn, backlog USD 561bn.
Alphabet Q3 2026 (reported): operating cash flow USD 42.3bn, capex USD 51.4bn, free cash flow minus USD 9.1bn reported, about minus USD 3.9bn excluding the USD 5.2bn EU fine.
Alphabet Q3 2026 (reported): Google Services operating margin 40.7%. Revenue grew 25% y/y, capex grew 114% y/y, depreciation rose 49%.
Alphabet 2026 capex guidance (company guidance): USD 195-205bn, with management flagging a significant increase in 2027.
Alphabet inventory (reported, end Q3 2026): USD 13.3bn versus USD 2.4bn at end 2025, driven by TPU system build.
risk_factors: Free cash flow turned negative as capex reaches 40% of revenue, with depreciation rising for years.
TPU contract ramp consumes cash ahead of delivery and billing, with cash return mostly in 2027.
Cloud margin faces Q4 headwinds from rented capacity and excludes USD 7.7bn of shared AI costs.
Customer concentration: a few large AI clients can negotiate prices or build their own chips, and several TPU clients compete with Google in models or cloud.
USD 924bn of purchase commitments and USD 152bn of leases not yet started, although some contracts allow lower volumes.
Buybacks have stopped, removing a significant part of the investment case for many holders.
Search growth has slowed while capex keeps accelerating.

tension_points.bull_case: Alphabet owns chips, cloud, models and distribution. Cloud revenue doubled to USD 30.7bn with a 36.2% margin and a USD 561bn backlog, and TPU systems have more than 100 significant external customers.
tension_points.bear_case: Free cash flow was minus USD 9.1bn, capex is 40% of revenue, buybacks have stopped, and Cloud is a competitive, capital-heavy business whose profit the market will not value like Search profit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: TPU inventory (USD 13.3bn) not converting into delivered and billed revenue by Q4 2026 results, a 2027 capex guidance increase that outpaces cash generation, or Cloud margin falling below 36% as rented capacity ramps.

theme_stances.key_argument: The full stack protects Alphabet's strategic position more than it answers the market's demand for cash.
